_: The words this system's public API is allowed to use, and what each one means.
A shared prop name is a promise: `tone` must mean the same thing on every
component that has it, or an agent that learned it once learns it wrong
everywhere else. This file is the promise written down; scripts/lint-vocab.mjs
is the promise enforced against the published profile.
A closed-union prop NAME used on two or more components and NOT declared here
is red: nobody has written down what the word means. A value outside its axis
is red too. To clear either, put the word here with a sentence — the cost is a
sentence rather than a checkbox because a value nobody can describe in a
sentence is a value that will drift.
`axis` names the ONE question a prop answers. A prop name that answers two
different questions is two props wearing one name. A value written as an object
with `onlyOn: interactive` is allowed only on components that render their own
control — the difference between a destructive ACTION and a bad STATE.
`scoped: true` marks an axis whose words are a component-local look, not a
system-wide scale; its words are declared so the name is accounted for, but
they carry no promise across components and are not policed value-by-value.

size.axis: how much room this thing takes

values.warning: it needs attention but nothing is broken
values.danger: it is broken, failed, or over a limit
values.ai: produced by a model rather than a person

destructive.why: a destructive ACTION is not a bad STATE: a button says `destructive`, a badge or a bar says `danger`. Allowing the action word on a display component is how a status ends up wearing it. Only IconButton carries it, and it renders a real control.

variant.axis: how much emphasis this CONTROL carries, and what role it plays

values.primary: the one action the screen wants
values.ghost: an action with no surface until hover
values.quiet: an action with no surface at all
values.filled: an action carrying a solid tone
values.dark: it sits on a dark surface
values.link: it navigates and looks like text

surface.axis: what this thing is sitting ON, so it can stay visible against it

values.base: the default surface — a card or the page body; a form control draws its resting border here
values.muted: the tinted surface; a control drops its resting border and lets its fill do the separating
values.card: inside a card, on white — a block that sizes itself to that surface
values.page: on the grey page body — the same block on the other surface

placement.axis: where a SURFACE sits against its trigger or the viewport

values.start: before the trigger in reading order (left in LTR, right in RTL)
values.end: after the trigger in reading order

values.circle: a round box: a person's avatar, a round control
values.square: a rounded rectangle where a circle is the default: a team or an organisation rather than a person

as.axis: which HTML element this renders as, when the choice is the document's and not the component's

values.span: inline text with no block semantics

appearance.axis: which of this component's own local visual styles it wears

values.meta: MetaItem: a run of secondary metadata
values.eyebrow: MetaItem: a small label above a heading
values.underline: Tabs: an underline under the active tab
values.pills: Tabs: each tab as a filled pill

align.axis: which edge of the thing it hangs from lines up

values.start: flush with the leading edge — left in a left-to-right reading order
values.center: centred on the thing it hangs from

density.axis: how much air sits between the rows of a thing that repeats

values.comfortable: the default — reading spacing, for a surface somebody dwells on
values.compact: tightened, for a surface being scanned rather than read
values.dense: as tight as the type allows, for the most data on one screen

columns.axis: how many columns the content is laid out across

values.1: one column — the stacked form, and what every layout falls back to when narrow
values.12: the twelve-column grid a page region is placed on, not a count of content columns
